data.situation:
The public affairs exhibition opened in the centre's upstairs room. Maya stopped beside a model parliament, where rows of seats faced a small speaking desk. The display described a fictional republic whose president was its head of state. Its legislature made laws, and its elected parliament debated proposals in the chamber. A ballot beside the model listed three candidates in an election. Maya chose a name, then realised that the candidate's campaign promise was a proposal to reform the transport system, rather than a power to change every rule alone. Noor moved a card from the speaking desk to the voting tray. In this model, a proposal needed support before it could become law. The next visitor wanted to know whether all countries arranged these institutions in the same way. Noor turned the diagram over: its reverse invited visitors to compare other systems instead of treating the model as a universal description. Model republic
The president is the head of state. The parliament shown here is an elected legislature. A candidate may promise to reform a system, but election to office does not by itself turn a proposal into law. Institutional arrangements differ across countries; this diagram describes the exhibition's fictional example. Maya: This candidate wants to reform public transport. Can she simply announce the change?
Noor: Not in our model. The proposal goes to parliament.
Maya: So I should distinguish her promise from the decision.
Noor: Exactly. Move the proposal card to the speaking desk, then follow the arrows to the vote.

readingBlocks.en: The public affairs exhibition opened in the centre's upstairs room. Maya stopped beside a model parliament, where rows of seats faced a small speaking desk. The display described a fictional republic whose president was its head of state. Its legislature made laws, and its elected parliament debated proposals in the chamber. A ballot beside the model listed three candidates in an election. Maya chose a name, then realised that the candidate's campaign promise was a proposal to reform the transport system, rather than a power to change every rule alone. Noor moved a card from the speaking desk to the voting tray. In this model, a proposal needed support before it could become law. The next visitor wanted to know whether all countries arranged these institutions in the same way. Noor turned the diagram over: its reverse invited visitors to compare other systems instead of treating the model as a universal description.
readingBlocks.zh: 公共事务展在社区中心楼上的房间开幕。玛雅停在议会模型旁，成排座位面向一张小发言桌。展板介绍一个虚构共和国，总统是国家元首，立法机关制定法律，民选议会在议事厅讨论提案。模型旁的选票列出选举中的三位候选人。玛雅选了一个名字，随后意识到，候选人竞选时承诺的是改革交通系统的提案，并不是独自改变所有规则的权力。努尔把一张卡从发言桌移到表决盘。在这个模型中，提案需要获得支持，才能成为法律。下一位参观者想知道所有国家是否都这样安排机构。努尔翻过结构图，背面邀请大家比较其他制度，而不是把这个模型视为普遍描述。

readingBlocks.en:
Model republic
The president is the head of state. The parliament shown here is an elected legislature. A candidate may promise to reform a system, but election to office does not by itself turn a proposal into law. Institutional arrangements differ across countries; this diagram describes the exhibition's fictional example.
readingBlocks.zh:
共和国模型
总统是国家元首。这里展示的议会是民选立法机关。候选人可以承诺改革某个系统，但当选本身不意味着提案已成为法律。不同国家的机构安排有所不同，此图描述的是展览中的虚构例子。

readingBlocks.en:
Maya: This candidate wants to reform public transport. Can she simply announce the change?
Noor: Not in our model. The proposal goes to parliament.
Maya: So I should distinguish her promise from the decision.
Noor: Exactly. Move the proposal card to the speaking desk, then follow the arrows to the vote.
readingBlocks.zh:
玛雅：这位候选人想改革公共交通，能直接宣布变更吗？
努尔：在我们的模型里不能。提案要提交议会。
玛雅：所以应该区分她的承诺和最后决定。
努尔：对，把提案卡移到发言桌，再沿箭头走到表决处。

glossary.note: 名词；stand in an election / win an election。
glossary.example: The ballot listed three candidates in an election.
glossary.exampleZh: 选票列出选举中的三位候选人。

externalEvidence.definition: a vote to select the winner of a position or political office

glossary.note: 名词，指国家的议会机构；不同国家的组成和权力不同。

externalEvidence.definition: a legislative assembly in certain countries

glossary.note: candidate in an election；也可指求职者，本事件使用选举义。
glossary.example: This candidate wants to reform public transport.
glossary.exampleZh: 这位候选人想改革公共交通。

externalEvidence.definition: a politician who is running for public office

glossary.note: 本句是国家职位；与协会或公司负责人用义分开。
glossary.example: The president is the head of state in the model republic.
glossary.exampleZh: 模型共和国的总统是国家元首。

externalEvidence.definition: the chief executive of a republic

glossary.note: 可数名词；本例说明机构职能，不保证所有立法机关均为民选。
glossary.example: The parliament shown here is an elected legislature.
glossary.exampleZh: 这里展示的议会是民选立法机关。

externalEvidence.definition: persons who make or amend or repeal laws

glossary.note: 及物动词 reform a system；本条采用动词义，名词 a reform 另有结构。
glossary.example: The candidate proposed to reform the transport system.
glossary.exampleZh: 候选人提议改革交通系统。

externalEvidence.definition: improve by alteration or correction of errors or defects and put into a better condition

retrievalPrompts.function: A ballot beside the model chamber
retrievalPrompts.cue: Explain the roles of the institutions in the model republic to a visitor.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 向参观者说明模型中的两个机构。
acceptableAnswers: In this model republic, the president is the head of state, while parliament is the elected legislature.

retrievalPrompts.function: A ballot beside the model chamber
retrievalPrompts.cue: Describe the people on the ballot and what one of them proposes.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 说明选票上的人物与承诺。
acceptableAnswers: The ballot lists three candidates in the election. One candidate proposes to reform public transport.

retrievalPrompts.function: A ballot beside the model chamber
retrievalPrompts.cue: Distinguish a campaign promise from a decision already in force in one sentence.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 写一句话，区分竞选承诺与已生效决定。
acceptableAnswers: The candidate has promised to reform the system, but the proposal still needs to be debated in parliament.

transferPrompt.function: A ballot beside the model chamber
transferPrompt.cue: A student-election candidate promises to change the activity timetable. Report the promise without suggesting the change has been approved.
transferPrompt.cueZh: 学生会选举有人承诺修改活动安排，向同学描述承诺而不说它已生效。
acceptableAnswers: A candidate in the student election has proposed to reform the activity timetable. The proposal still needs approval.
